gloss: to resume; to reopen; to restart

definitions.gloss: to resume; to reopen; to restart
definitions.explanation: To begin again something that had been stopped, suspended, or closed. Used for activities, services, operations, and negotiations.

examples.japanese: {授業|じゅぎょう}を{再開|さいかい}する。
{工事|こうじ}は{来月|らいげつ}{再開|さいかい}される{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: Construction is scheduled to resume next month.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{休業|きゅうぎょう}の{後|あと}、あの{店|みせ}がようやく{営業|えいぎょう}を{再開|さいかい}した。
examples.english: After a long closure, that shop finally reopened for business.

notes:
{再開|さいかい}する combines {再|さい} (again) and {開|かい} (open), meaning to open or start something again after an interruption. It is used for both transitive (to resume something) and intransitive (something resumes) patterns.

USAGE:
- ～を{再開|さいかい}する: to resume something (transitive)
- ～が{再開|さいかい}する/される: something resumes (intransitive/passive)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {営業|えいぎょう}を{再開|さいかい}する: to reopen for business
- {運転|うんてん}を{再開|さいかい}する: to resume service (trains, etc.)
- {交渉|こうしょう}を{再開|さいかい}する: to resume negotiations
- {活動|かつどう}を{再開|さいかい}する: to resume activities
- {工事|こうじ}を{再開|さいかい}する: to restart construction

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {再|さい}スタートする: to restart — more casual, often used for personal endeavors or career restarts
- {復活|ふっかつ}する: to revive; to come back — implies revival from a dead or defunct state, stronger than {再開|さいかい}
- {続|つづ}ける: to continue — implies no interruption occurred, unlike {再開|さいかい} which presupposes a break
